originality.rationale: The nontrivial claim is a universal Ω(log N) lower bound on radial levels for any positive weighted sampler, matched by a finite dyadic-radius construction with uniform analytic frame constants. Verified accessible prior sampling papers give geometric sufficient and sampling-family conditions, not this resource necessity. Classical positive exponential approximations cover the construction paradigm but inspected McLean 2016 does not state the universal radial lower bound. A closely related Fock sampling theorem has Gaussian moments and Θ(sqrt N), not beta moments. Best-knowledge originality only; an older stronger exponential-sum result could cover it.

value.rationale: Radial-level count is a natural resource in circular samplers, distinct from total nodes. The unrestricted lower bound and explicit upper family yield matching Θ(log N) order over all fixed β>0, a complete asymptotic geometric resource law, not merely a constant improvement. Novelty rests in the arbitrary-positive sampler necessity rather than the already-known general exponential-sum upper construction.
